subject: MedNext onboarding: model shortlist, context needs, and token traffic ops

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: CS handoff: MedNext pilot kickoff — context and asks

Hi Grace,

Handoff for MedNext (Paul Simon / Sarah Liao) — they want to run a 6-week pilot for chart summarization that will surface the single best paragraph summary and a structured list of extracted items for clinician triage. Key facts:

- Primary contact: Paul Simon (product) and Sarah Liao (ops).
- Expected pilot traffic: ~2M tokens/month initially, spiking to ~5M in weekends of internal testing.
- Typical user flow: 1) clinician uploads chart (avg 1,800 chars), 2) pipeline sends a prompt + chart context (~180 tokens prompt + ~400 tokens context avg), 3) model returns ~350 token summary + 70 token structured list.
- Latency target: p95 <= 350ms for UI surface (they prefer <250ms but will accept up to 350ms during pilot).
- Security: data residency in US, SOC2 required (they've requested audit logs).

They asked us to recommend 2-3 model variants (fast/cost/quality) and an initial traffic plan including batching/KV caching suggestions. Can you coordinate the CS->Implementation kickoff and confirm which model variants we'll test in week 1 vs fallback for overload?

Attachments: MedNext MVP doc and sample contexts (sent inline).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

- Ben: please draft initial capacity profile (concurrency, qps, burst) based on the token numbers below.

1) Model shortlist + tradeoffs (quality vs cost vs latency)
2) Preliminary token & throughput profile (expected peak qps, concurrency needs)
3) Quick ops plan: KV caching for repeated charts, batching thresholds, and fallback routing policy.

Monica — can you aim to have the shortlist + recommended config by tomorrow morning?

-Grace

Thanks for the quick handoff. A couple clarifications from our side before the kickoff:

- The "chart" payloads are usually ~1–2 sections; effective context we care about is the last 10 notes (~350–600 tokens) rather than the full file. So you can assume ~450 tokens of context on average.
- We have scheduled internal stress-tests next Wednesday and expect a short burst that could triple baseline qps for up to 45 minutes.
- Acceptance criteria: 1) summary captures 95% of key findings on a blinded eval set, 2) p95 latency under 350ms for the UI path.

We can share a small 500-record sample for metric evaluation.

-Paul

Subject: Re: CS handoff: MedNext pilot kickoff — shortlist & sizing proposal

Folks — draft recommendations below (shortlist + sizing). Will bring this to the kickoff and capture any customer constraints.

Model shortlist (week 1 -> week 2 -> fallback):
- Candidate A (Quality-first): redwood-instruct-v3-13B (float16) — best summary quality, expected p95 180–260ms at single-request latency, estimated cost: high.
- Candidate B (Cost-optimized): redwood-instruct-v3-7B-8q (8-bit quantized) — good quality for structured extraction, p95 ~220–320ms, ~45% cheaper token cost in our estimation.
- Fallback variant: redwood-chat-3-small (low-cost, low-latency) as an emergency route when capacity is constrained.

Assumptions & token math (per call average):
- Prompt template + system instr: 180 tokens
- Context: 450 tokens (customer clarified)
- Model output: summary 350 tokens + structured list 70 tokens = 420 tokens
- Total tokens per call = 1,050 tokens (round up to 1,100 for headroom)

Traffic & capacity: baseline expected calls: 2,000 calls/day (~60 calls/hr average) = ~2.2M tokens/month (matches Marissa's estimate). Peak stress test: 3x burst = ~6,000 calls/day for the day of test.

Throughput profile (initial):
- Average qps: 0.7 (60 calls/hr -> 1 call per minute = 0.0167 qps, but steady distributed daytime usage yields ~0.7 qps accounting for concurrency across users)
- Peak qps during stress: target 12–25 qps (we need reserve headroom).
- Concurrency: plan for baseline concurrency 8 and burst headroom up to 40 (scale with Dedicated or Hosted burst).

Ops recommendations:
- KV/prefix caching: cache recent chart contexts keyed by patient ID to avoid re-sending identical blocks for minor UI edits. Expect 10–18% token savings initially.
- Batching: allow small micro-batching up to 2–3 requests for background summarization tasks (UI path should avoid batching >1 for latency).
- Quantization: test candidate B in week 2 to assert quality delta; if acceptable, shift 60% of non-critical calls to the quantized variant.
- Fallback routing: route to redwood-chat-3-small if production p95 > 400ms or if model A queueing > 30s.

SLA / monitoring hooks to add for pilot:
- Per-route p50/p95 latency, token consumption per call, and quality regression alerts on evaluation set.
- Automatic canary: 10% of traffic to candidate B during week 2 before ramp.

Attachments: redwood-model-sieve.xlsx contains per-model microbenchmarks.

If that looks good I'll finalize the numbers and add the specific capacity sizing for the Dedicated pool (gpu counts / instance types) and a short runbook.

-Monica

--
Monica Patel

2) Ben: please include burst capacity numbers and an optional Dedicated trial estimate (monthly) in the runbook.
3) Paul/Sarah: please upload the 500-record sample to the Drive link above and confirm the two users who should be part of the acceptance review.

I'll attach the MVP acceptance doc and the ops runbook after the call. Looking forward to it.
